newsitem.title: USA: Fibreboard sees $4/shr gain on resort sale.
newsitem.headline: Fibreboard sees $4/shr gain on resort sale.

text.p: Fibreboard Corp said Tuesday it has signed a letter of intent to sell all the assets of its Resorts Group, which will net the company about $4 per share.
Fibreboard said it plans to sell the resorts Northstar-at-Tahoe, Sierra-at-Tahoe and Bear Mountain to Booth Creek Inc, a corporation formed by George Gillett.

A total of about $127 million will be realized from the sale, Fibreboard said in a press release, noting that the purchase price is subject to adjustment based on working capital levels and transaction timing.
Fibreboard estimates after-tax cash proceeds of $90 to $95 million. The gain for financial reporting purposes is expected to be in the range of $33 to $38 million, or about $4 per share.
The deal is subject to the execution of a definitive purchase agreement and regulatory approval. It is expected to close by November 30, Fibreboard said.
After the sale, Fibreboard will have a net-cash position of about $40 million and what it called "substantial borrowing power to fund an aggressive acquisition program."
The Resort Group sale will be accounted for as a discontinued operation and financial statements for prior periods will be restated.
In the month of December 1995, the Resort Group contributed $900,000 in operating earnings, equivalent to $600,000 after-tax or $0.07 per share, the company said.
For the first quarter of 1996, the Resort Group contributed operating earnings of $9.3 million, equivalent to $5.6 million after-tax or $0.62 per share.
